findings.text: — §1 defines its population twice with two different criteria: "every open decision that waits on the lead" and "an open decision already written in a plan's decisions block appears in the same read". An unset `data-choice` carries no evidence that any work waits on it, so the second arm admits decisions with no held work and no requester; measured in the mounted projects today, unset decisions are 62 across five projects (reckon 25, imas-codex 15, imas-ambix 11, nova 10, imas-efit 1), against the single decision the Why paragraph names as actually waiting ("the basis choice for iron-core-magnetisation §5", `formulation`, the only unset entry of its three examples). §4 then presents "every open decision to the lead", so the surface opens on roughly 62 mostly-draft entries and the lead has no way to read which of them holds work — and the plan names no criterion that could decide it. The system already holds such a criterion: a plan decision is what a node's `requires_decisions` names, and a node whose required decision is unlocked is refused (reckon/crew/node.py:808, :1487) — work is then genuinely held behind that decision. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: without a stated criterion the §1 worker picks one (all unset decisions, or only held records), and §1's measure and §4's presentation measure different populations depending on which reading the worker took.

— §1's deliverable is "One read", yet its done-when requires three recorded decisions holding four, one and zero queued requests read back "with every field present and the held requests named", which cannot be asserted without a record store and a writer; §2 then requires a hold to carry a record and §3 requires an answer to close one, so all three sections depend on a write path no section declares as its deliverable. The followup queues §1–§4 in one batch, so a §1 worker building the store by inference, a §2 worker building the record writer it needs for its hold, and a §3 worker building the close path can each implement a different one and merge cleanly. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: naming the store and its write path as a §1 deliverable (or as its own node ahead of §2) is what stops three concurrent workers from owning one mechanism.

— §3 states "Only an answer given through the presenting session is accepted; a session cannot answer a decision for itself or for another session", unqualified, while §1 puts plan-block decisions into the same read and those decisions are answered today by setting `data-choice` through the MCP `lock` op or POST /plan/<project>/<slug> — the path AGENTS.md mandates for decisions and the one a node's `requires_decisions` gate reads to release held work (reckon/crew/node.py:1487). Implemented literally, §3 either refuses that existing channel for every decision §1 surfaces, or has no subject for plan-block decisions and its stated guard never fires; the plan does not say which. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: an ambiguity between two of this plan's own sections decides whether §3 removes the repository's decision-locking path or governs only session-held records, and the two answers need different implementations and different controls.

response_events.note: The new section 5 separates the two populations in the read: a plan-block decision that holds no work is listed apart from the decisions that hold work, so the ready list is the decisions something waits on.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every named target resolves: nova/docs/plans/iron-core-magnetisation.html (§5 exists), kernel-compile-barrier.html, sub-millisecond-forward-path.html, docs/plans/work-flows-to-the-lane.html, skills/.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §1–§4 states a negative control that is executable at the base revision (read absent, a lead hold accepted with no record, `data-choice` written at base leaves the held request held, skill absent), and each names durable evidence and the all_debug tier.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — all four failing runs are logged to docs/evidence/fragments/lead-decisions-reach-one-place/sN.html, the one-HTML-document-under-the-plan-directory shape reckon/crew/reports.py accepts, not a node-local scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `reckon-select` and the record field names carry no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers; the slug appears only in the evidence path, which is the fragment convention rather than a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1 never defines which plan-block decision "waits on the lead", and the plan-block population it sweeps in is 62 unset decisions across five mounted projects, so the read's own quantity — the amount of held work — is unobtainable for that arm.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §1's done-when requires a decision store and a write path that §1's deliverable text never names.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-section-depends-on declares s2→s1, s3→s1, s4→{s1,s3}, which matches followup f-ldop-001 and the deliverable dependencies; plan-after work-flows-to-the-lane.html resolves.
